A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MLIP pre-training, Force2Geo and Force2Prop work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison despite substantial reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original backbone benchmarks, geometry-optimization evaluations, molecular property predictions and supplementary experiments, including the QM9 experiment in Appendix A.5.4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports backbone training times in Table 2 and configuration-convergence observations in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Equation (6) changes the stated force-training loss from mean squared vector error to its square root. The backbone, BFGS relaxation and geometry fine-tuning pipeline remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether the loss revision corrects documentation or reflects different executed training.

E1.justification: Both versions use PubChemQCR/PubChemQCR-S, Molecule3D subset and full-dataset evaluations, ∇2DFT, and the QM9 scenario without ground-truth training geometries. v2 Appendix A provides more information about the existing dataset, without establishing added data or task coverage.

E2.justification: The nine backbone comparators in Table 2, downstream prediction comparators, and coordinate-denoising/DeNS comparisons retain the same membership. Matching v1 Tables 8–12 to v2 Tables 9–13 reveals no added or removed comparison method.

E3.justification: Table 2 adds training time in minutes per epoch as an evaluation measure alongside energy MAE and force RMSE. Dataset splits and geometry-optimization stopping criteria are retained. Appendix C newly documents benchmark configurations and preprocessing, without establishing changes to previously executed settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds computational-efficiency evidence for backbone selection in Table 2 and reports failed convergence of larger Equiformer configurations in Appendix C. Existing feature-freezing, data-scaling, pre-training-strategy, noise, loss-weight and QM9 analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bars for the results. The coordinate-noise standard deviations are experimental hyperparameters, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds runtime results, including 26 minutes per epoch for PaiNN and 65 for Equiformer in Table 2, plus dataset-stage statistics and the Equiformer convergence-failure observation. Matched accuracy and relaxation-result tables retain their numerical values; the rescaled data-size plots preserve their results.

T1.justification: The square root added to Equation (6) changes the mathematical definition of the force loss. Other mathematical definitions and geometry-optimization metrics are retained apart from notation changes. No new theorem, proof or theoretical guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow the geometry-generation claim: outputs are explicitly approximate and need not achieve DFT-level chemical accuracy or convergence, although they can improve downstream prediction. The dataset, Force2Geo, geometry fine-tuning and Force2Prop contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly states that Force2Geo's usefulness depends on the molecular system and downstream task. Its new Broader Impact Statement cautions against treating generated geometries as DFT-quality structures in critical applications. Existing explanations involving low-force regimes and the QM9 distribution mismatch are retained.

D1.justification: v1 provides a brief dataset description and PaiNN training settings. v2 substantially expands reproducibility information through Appendix A's generation software, curation process and LMDB organization, and Appendix C/Table 8's per-model configurations, preprocessing, force heads, training budgets and hardware. It also supplies explicit code and dataset access links.

R1.justification: Section 3 adds an explicit discussion of conventional 3D GNN property predictors and their dependence on accurate geometries. The named methods were already cited and evaluated in v1, so this is a limited expansion of research positioning rather than new literature or comparator coverage.

P1.justification: v2 replaces 'foundation model' terminology throughout, itemizes the contributions, adds a Broader Impact Statement and reorganizes the appendices into Sections A–G. Most matched method, experiment and analysis prose remains substantially unchanged rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: The document receives a comprehensive journal-format redesign, including the author block, typography, margins, running headers and float placement. Table 2 gains a timing column and Table 8 adds configurations. The existing scaling plots exchange figure numbers and are redrawn with zero-based, common 0–0.12 vertical ranges.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the existing study easier to reproduce and assess through detailed dataset and benchmark documentation, access information and runtime measurements. Its qualified headline claims better reflect Table 3's unchanged 10.29% chemical-accuracy success and 4.2% force-convergence rates. These support a limited overall improvement, while the unexplained force-loss revision leaves uncertainty about the implemented objective.
